title: Score: a live refusal renders as a generic error; refused-silence UI is unreachable
body:
## Summary
Every refused-silence affordance on the Score step keys on `cue.status === "failed"`, a field that is absent by construction on every live cue. The session's real refusal (`take.state === "refused"`) gets none of them and renders identically to a network error.

## Description
`spots.ts:52` states `status` is absent by construction and `toCueSpots` (spots.ts:217-224) never sets it, so on the live surface `cue.status` is always undefined. Yet the step's refusal vocabulary is all gated on it: the rose dashed music-lane span (ScoreSpotting.tsx:827,836), the rose card border (:934), the `re-ask the model` button label (:1049-1050), the `kind=` chip (:989), and the refused-silence flatline (:1119). Meanwhile `renderCue`'s catch (:608-612) carefully separates `refused` from `error`, with the comment promising "the region reverts to refused-silence and the surface says so, in its own color" - and then :1110-1112 renders both with the same `text-rose-200/70` paragraph. Comment-as-spec diff: the promised distinction does not exist in the JSX. The failure line also has no live region, so a screen-reader user who pressed `render this cue` hears nothing when it fails (CutWorkbench.tsx:96 uses role="alert" for its trouble).

## Flow
- Creator sets a tempo, presses `render this cue`.
- Engine refuses (MusicRequestError code=refused) -> takes[cue] = {state:"refused"}.
- Card shows one rose line, button still reads `render this cue`, no flatline, span stays cyan/amber.
- Same render for a dropped connection (state "error").

## Expected impact
The one surface where money is spent tells a refusal (change the brief) apart from an outage (retry) only by message wording; the refused-silence picture built for exactly this case is dead code in production.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refused take is drawn as refused-silence, distinct from an error.
Before: branches reading `take?.state === "refused"` distinctly from "error" = 0; refusal affordances reachable on a live cue = 0 of 5 (all key on cue.status, always undefined).
After: a derived `refused = cue.status === "failed" || take?.state === "refused"` drives the 5 affordances; error take renders with role="alert" in a distinct tone.
Method: probe - source ratchet over stripped ScoreSpotting.tsx.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/_phases/score/spots.ts:52 (`status` is absent by construction); spots.ts:217-224 toCueSpots copies id,title,sceneIds,note,bpm only; app/_phases/score/ScoreSpotting.tsx:608-612 refused vs error split; :1110-1112 one shared

for both; :1119 flatline gated on cue.status==='failed'; :934 card border, :1049-1050 're-ask the model', :827/:836 span tone, :989 kind chip - all on cue.status; grep 'take?.state === "refused"' in ScoreSpotting.tsx -> only :1110 (OR'd with error). Sibling: app/_phases/cut/CutWorkbench.tsx:96 role="alert".
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/score-refusal-state.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(ScoreSpotting.tsx); assert (a) the flatline/card-border/button-label conditions reference take state 'refused' (e.g. a `refused` const that includes `take?.state === "refused"`), and (b) the error-take branch is a separate element carrying role="alert" and not sharing the refused branch. Red on HEAD (only one shared branch at :1110), green after. Existing tests/golden-path/music-cue-provenance.probe.spec.ts must stay green (engineCredit untouched). npm run typecheck.

title: Frames header says '0 frames derived' on every trailer, beside a full shot sheet
body:
## Summary
On any non-explainer project the Frames header reads `0 frames derived from "<title>" (<engineLabel>)`, and the engineLabel itself narrates the app (`... - see the shots view`, `no spine composed yet - Step 2 composes it`).

## Description
FramesStep.tsx:73-79 records the defect it fixed: a promotional cut has `frames = []` by construction (frames.ts:399-401), and drawing a 0/0 ledger "reads as nothing done yet when the truth is this step does not work that way here". The view is now forced to `shots`, but the header line at :155-157 still prints `{ctl.frames.length} frames derived` - `0 frames` - directly above a ShotSheet that tallies e.g. `SHOTS 24 · BEATS 9`. Two counts of the same film disagree on one screen. The parenthesised engineLabel for those origins is app-subject prose: frames.ts:354 `"<template> · N beats - see the shots view"` (the app telling you where to click; the locked tabs already say it) and frames.ts:380 `"no spine composed yet - Step 2 composes it"` (restating the <UpstreamBreak> ShotSheet.tsx:147 draws right below).

## Flow
- Open Frames on a trailer project -> tabs lock to `shots`.
- Header: `0 frames derived from "Pier 7" (Trailer · 9 beats - see the shots view)`.
- Below: `DERIVED  SHOTS 24  BEATS 9`.

## Expected impact
Removes a false zero and two app-narrating clauses from the first line of the step on every promotional project.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the header never states a zero frame count for a cut that has no frame layer.
Before: on origins trailer-cut and no-spine the header renders `0 frames derived` (frames.length===0 by frames.ts:400) + 2 narrating engineLabel strings.
After: the `frames derived` line rendered only when `!promotionalCut` (explainer-fixture); engineLabel strings at frames.ts:354/:380 reduced to work facts (template · N beats) with the `see the shots view` / `Step 2 composes it` clauses deleted.
Method: probe - source ratchet.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/frames/FramesStep.tsx:155-157 `{ctl.frames.length} frames derived from ...({ctl.render.engineLabel})` rendered unconditionally; :87-88 promotionalCut forces view 'shots'; app/_phases/frames/frames.ts:399-401 framesFor returns [] for any origin but explainer-fixture; frames.ts:354 engineLabel `... beats — see the shots view`; frames.ts:380 `no spine composed yet — Step 2 composes it`; app/_phases/frames/ShotSheet.tsx:147-153 UpstreamBreak already drawn for no-spine, :213-214 Tally shots/beats.
verify: Probe tests/golden-path/frames-header-count.probe.spec.ts: (1) stripComments(FramesStep.tsx) - the `frames derived` text sits inside a branch guarded by promotionalCut / origin === 'explainer-fixture'; (2) stripComments(frames.ts): no string contains 'see the shots view' or 'Step 2 composes'. Red on HEAD, green after. Then npm run typecheck && npm run check:narration; photograph studio-frames on a trailer project via pipeline/cx-capture.mjs.

title: Unsourced figure has four names and two unlabeled amber dots
body:
## Summary
One concept - a figure text bound to no notebook fact - is spelled four ways on one screen, and its two on-canvas/on-list markers are a bare `●` whose only name is a native `title`.

## Description
FramesAssembly.tsx:146 header `N unsourced figure(s)`; FramesAssembly.tsx:418 select option `— cites no fact —`; parts.tsx:335 canvas dot title `not bound to a notebook fact`; LayerPanel.tsx:178 list dot title `figure with no fact behind it`. The header is the integrity number the step "exists to catch" (comment :143-144), yet a reader cannot match it to the dots by word. Accessibility: both dots are colour+glyph only; `title` on a non-focusable span is not reliably exposed, so LayerPanel's row button announces as `figure 42% ●` and the canvas mark as `42% ●`. Per the vocabulary law the fix is one word reused, not more prose: the header already chose `unsourced`.

## Flow
- Add a figure text, leave it unbound.
- Header: `1 unsourced figure`; canvas: amber ● (hover: "not bound to a notebook fact"); layer list: amber ● (hover: "figure with no fact behind it"); select: "— cites no fact —".

## Expected impact
One term across the step; the warning reaches non-visual users.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the unbound-figure state has one name and an accessible name on every marker.
Before: 4 distinct strings for the concept; 2 `●` markers with title-only naming and no sr-only text.
After: 1 term (`unsourced`) in all four sites; both markers aria-hidden glyph + sr-only `unsourced` (or role="img" aria-label="unsourced figure"); the two `title=` attributes removed.
Method: probe - grep count + source ratchet.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/frames/FramesAssembly.tsx:146 'unsourced figure'; :418 '— cites no fact —'; app/_phases/frames/parts.tsx:334-337 ●; app/_phases/frames/LayerPanel.tsx:177-181 ●. Neither ● carries aria-label/sr-only.
verify: Probe: stripComments over the three files; assert the strings 'not bound to a notebook fact', 'figure with no fact behind it', 'cites no fact' occur 0 times (HEAD: 3), and that each `●` in parts.tsx and LayerPanel.tsx is aria-hidden with an adjacent sr-only 'unsourced' (or role=img + aria-label containing 'unsourced'). npm run check:narration must not rise (removes 2 title= attributes).

title: Frames batch: 'budget ceiling reached' never says when, and never re-arms
body:
## Summary
When the imaging budget is exhausted the batch button goes dead with `budget ceiling reached` and no time, while the sibling paused state on the same button says `paused until HH:MM`. The quote is never re-fetched when the window rolls over, so the button stays dead until a reload.

## Description
`planRender` (renderPlan.ts) returns `resumeAt` for the `blocked` and `partial` verdicts, sourced from lib/imaging/budgetForecast.ts:94-98, and its header promises "resume time". FramesAssembly reads only `plan.count` and `plan.label` (:92, :164, :174); `plan.resumeAt` has zero consumers in app/ (grep). The quote effect (:58-69) depends only on `missing.length` - which a blocked batch cannot change - so after the window expires the button still reads `budget ceiling reached`, disabled. Pair: the mid-batch pause branch (:170-171) renders `paused until ${toLocaleTimeString()}` for the same cause (over-budget, afterOutcome pause-until).

## Flow
- Budget spent -> quote verdict blocked -> button `budget ceiling reached` (disabled), no time.
- Window rolls over -> nothing changes; user must reload to find out.

## Expected impact
Removes a dead end on the most expensive control in the step; one cause, one wording, with the time.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a blocked batch states when it resumes and re-arms at that time.
Before: consumers of plan.resumeAt in app/ = 0; quote refetch triggers = missing.length only.
After: blocked label appends ` · resumes HH:MM` from plan.resumeAt (same toLocaleTimeString as :171); a timeout at resumeAt re-runs quoteBudget (cleared on unmount / dependency change).
Method: probe - source ratchet over FramesAssembly.tsx.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn resumeAt app/ lib/ -> only app/_phases/frames/renderPlan.ts and lib/imaging/budgetForecast.ts, lib/imagingClient.ts; app/_phases/frames/FramesAssembly.tsx:58-69 effect deps [missing.length]; :71-74 planRender; :164 disabled when plan.count===0; :168-174 label chain uses plan.label, paused branch :170-171 prints time; renderPlan.ts blocked -> {count:0,label:'budget ceiling reached',resumeAt}.
verify: Probe tests/golden-path/frames-budget-resume.probe.spec.ts: stripComments(FramesAssembly.tsx) contains `plan.resumeAt` at least twice (label + re-quote timer) and a setTimeout/clearTimeout pair inside the quote effect keyed on resumeAt. Red on HEAD (0 occurrences). Existing tests/golden-path/imaging-budget-forecast.probe.spec.ts stays green (renderPlan.ts untouched). npm run typecheck && npm run lint:ratchet (no set-state-in-effect added: set state only inside timer/then callbacks).

title: Frames layers: unnamed text input and N identical 'Remove layer' names
body:
## Summary
In the expanded assembly row every text layer's value input has no accessible name, and every LayerPanel row's four icon buttons announce identical names (`Bring forward`, `Send backward`, `Hide layer`, `Remove layer`) regardless of which layer they act on.

## Description
FramesAssembly.tsx:391-395 `<input value={t.value} ...>` has no aria-label, no placeholder and no <label>; the role word beside it (:390) is a plain span. A screen reader announces "edit text, 42%". The sibling remove button two lines below does it right: aria-label `Remove ${t.role}` (:398). LayerPanel.tsx:184-195 gives every row's controls the same four names, so a list of five layers exposes five `Remove layer` buttons - destructive and indistinguishable in a buttons list. The row's own `name` (:174) is in scope and unused. Visual pair (observation, not this fix): those icons sit at text-white/25 and the disabled arrows at disabled:opacity-20, ~0.05 effective alpha on the ink ground.

## Flow
- Expand a row -> Tab into texts -> "edit text" (no name).
- Open the layer list in a buttons rotor -> "Remove layer" x5.

## Expected impact
Each control says what it edits/removes; the destructive button is identifiable.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every layer control carries a name that includes its layer.
Before: unnamed inputs in FramesAssembly text rows = 1 per text; LayerPanel aria-labels interpolating the layer = 0 of 4.
After: input aria-label `${t.role} text`; LayerPanel labels `Remove ${name}` / `Hide ${name}` / `Bring ${name} forward` / `Send ${name} backward`.
Method: probe - source ratchet.
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/frames/FramesAssembly.tsx:391-395 input without aria-label/placeholder; :396-398 sibling Remove button aria-label `Remove ${t.role}`; app/_phases/frames/LayerPanel.tsx:184,187,190,193 static aria-labels 'Bring forward'/'Send backward'/'Hide layer'|'Show layer'/'Remove layer'; `name` prop available at :133/:174.
verify: Probe: stripComments(LayerPanel.tsx) - every aria-label in Row is a template literal containing `${name}` (HEAD: 0 of 4); stripComments(FramesAssembly.tsx) - the `<input` with `value={t.value}` carries aria-label. Red on HEAD, green after. npm run typecheck.
